title: C5 worker manifest
description: /tmp/tsb/workers/{worker_id}.json. Written by the worker, atomically (a temporary file renamed over the old one), on every change; left in place if the worker crashes. It is how a restarted core rediscovers a worker it did not spawn, through the filesystem interface (immortality §2.1, Contract §8): for each connection, dial {conn_dir}/control.sock, and {conn_dir}/{socket} for each session. Liveness is that dial: a socket that is missing or refuses the connection belongs to a dead worker. pid is informational only — meaningful inside the writer's PID namespace, and the worker runs in its own container. It carries no credential. Closed: a worker writes exactly the fields of its tag. proto_version is absent from every v0.1 manifest, and that absence is how a v0.2 core recognises a v0.1 worker. A retained ended session (ipc-control.schema.json release) stays listed, with its socket, until the core releases it or its connection closes. A restarted v0.2 core rediscovers in this order (c5-rediscovery-v0.2): it reads the spool first (spool-entry.schema.json), because a worker that ended a session while the core was away may since have exited; it dials as v0.1 does — a socket that is missing or refuses is a dead worker, terminated / worker_lost, whatever the manifest's version, unless the spool holds that session's end (a worker the core cannot reach is a dead worker, decision 5.38); then, for a live peer only, it branches on proto_version: none → the sessions are unreachable / protocol (immortality §6.4: never silently killed); any version → the handshake (ipc-control.schema.json hello), with the core's own version when it does not know the worker's. A listed retained ended session is replayed by that handshake before the core writes its spooled end. The v0.1 rule (c5-rediscovery: liveness is the dial) is unchanged.

proto_version.description: The C3 version this worker speaks; "0.8" at this tag. Optional so a v0.1 manifest stays valid, and its absence is how a core recognises one.

connections.description: N connections per worker (immortality §2.2, LOCKED): a pool, even when N is configured to 1.
